issues.title: Phase 1: coarse layerwise ablation and causal localization
issues.body:
## Objective

Implement and run the first coarse-grained ablation to determine where LLM-vs-EC divergence first appears.

## Layers

- S1 Language -> Domain Semantics
- S2 Domain Semantics -> Candidate Set
- S3 Candidate Set -> Selection / Reframing
- S4 Selected State -> Execution / Closure

## Required comparison conditions

A. LLM generation + LLM selection/control
B. LLM generation + EC selection/control
C. Fixed candidate set + LLM selection/control
D. Fixed candidate set + EC selection/control
E. Oracle substitution at each layer

## Required measurements

- Semantic Recall
- Candidate Recall
- Correct Candidate Rank
- Selection Accuracy
- Residual Recall
- Reframing Recovery Rate
- False Closure Rate
- Missed Reframe Rate
- Final Task Success
- token/compute/latency cost where measurable

## Method

1. Freeze fixtures and artifact schemas before comparison.
2. Persist every layer output and hash it.
3. Hold upstream artifacts identical when comparing a downstream layer.
4. Substitute one layer at a time.
5. Measure Oracle substitution gain.
6. Select only the highest-materiality layer for further decomposition.
7. Do not infer layer causality from end-to-end score alone.

## Acceptance criteria

Follow `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md`, especially AC-01 through AC-20.

## Constraints

- Large LLM is not required for Phase 1.
- Prefer fixed fixtures + lightweight LLM + deterministic EC + Oracle.
- Cache LLM outputs for replay.
- Do not enable GitHub Actions.

## Exit condition

Phase 1 closes when the dominant divergence layer has been localized with a controlled intervention and is ready to be decomposed into finer sublayers.

issues.title: Phase 1: freeze fixture, oracle, and layer artifact contracts
issues.body:
## Objective

Freeze the comparison contract before any LLM-vs-EC measurement so causal attribution cannot be invalidated by moving layer boundaries, oracle definitions, or fixture semantics.

## Required artifacts

- `docs/PHASE1_FIXTURE_ORACLE_CONTRACT.md`
- `schemas/task_input.schema.json`
- `schemas/s1_domain_semantic_ir.schema.json`
- `schemas/s2_candidate_set.schema.json`
- `schemas/s3_selected_reframed_state.schema.json`
- `schemas/s4_closure_execution_result.schema.json`
- `schemas/fixture_manifest.schema.json`
- `fixtures/phase1_v1/`

## Required fixture content

Each fixture must persist:

1. task input
2. S1 oracle domain-semantic IR
3. S2 oracle candidate set
4. S3 oracle selection/reframing state
5. S4 oracle closure/execution result
6. fixture manifest

## Acceptance criteria

- S1-S4 have fixed machine-readable input/output contracts.
- LLM, EC, and Oracle can consume the exact same persisted upstream artifact.
- Oracle references are implementation-independent.
- Multiple valid semantic outputs can be represented by constraints rather than exact text.
- Every artifact records schema version, fixture generation, artifact identity, source refs, and hash field.
- Upstream hashes are identical across controlled downstream comparisons.
- At least 10 fixture slots cover direct semantics, near-miss concepts, multi-candidate cases, superficial winners, reframe/no-reframe, false closure, valid closure, multiple-valid-output, and domain-language ambiguity.
- Any semantic change after freeze requires a new fixture generation; results may not be mixed across generations.
- No GitHub Actions are enabled.

## Current progress

The contract and all S1-S4/manifest schemas are present. The first fixture `P1-001-direct-semantic` is complete as a DRAFT with task + S1-S4 oracle + manifest.

## Exit condition

Issue closes when the contract is stable enough to instantiate all 10 fixtures without schema changes, then the fixture generation is populated, validated explicitly, hashed, and frozen before Phase 1 measurement.

issues.title: TCC finding: P1-003 multi-candidate oracle under-represents valid branches
issues.body:
## Found during

ECv4.4-aligned TCC qualification of the Phase 1 fixture contract.

## Finding

`P1-003-multi-candidate` states that two candidate branches satisfy the domain constraints, but the current oracle representation exposes fewer than two `acceptable_candidate_ids`.

## Why this matters

This would confound Candidate Recall and Selection Accuracy: a model generating the second valid branch could be incorrectly penalized by the oracle.

## Required repair

- Add a second semantically valid candidate to the S2 oracle.
- Include both valid candidates in the acceptable set.
- Ensure S3 selection/oracle constraints can represent both without forcing surface-form identity.
- Re-run schema + semantic qualification before freeze.

## TCC result

Initial qualification: `BLOCKED`; 60 artifacts structurally validated; 1 blocking semantic residual detected.

GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: TCC finding: generated artifact hashes become stale after upstream-hash linkage
issues.body:
## Found during

ECv4.4-aligned qualification before Phase 1 freeze.

## Finding

`tools/generate_phase1_fixtures.py` computes `content_hash` for S1-S4, then writes `semantic_ir_hash`, `candidate_set_hash`, and `selected_state_hash` into S2-S4. That mutates S2-S4 after their canonical hashes were computed, so the recorded hashes become stale.

## Impact

A controlled downstream comparison could claim an upstream artifact identity that does not actually match the persisted artifact bytes/semantic object. This breaks the freeze and replay contract.

## Required repair

1. Compute S1 hash first.
2. Set S2 `semantic_ir_hash`, then compute S2 hash.
3. Set S3 `candidate_set_hash`, then compute S3 hash.
4. Set S4 `selected_state_hash`, then compute S4 hash.
5. Extend TCC validation to recompute each artifact hash and verify the chain.
6. Re-run qualification before freeze.

GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase 1 blocker: measurement fixtures leak oracle scenario labels
issues.body:
## Found during

Start of Issue #1 coarse ablation using ECv4.4/TCC.

## Finding

The Phase 1 task input generated by `tools/generate_phase1_fixtures.py` includes `context.scenario` values such as `reframe-required`, `false-closure-trap`, `valid-closure`, and `multiple-valid-outputs`. These labels directly reveal the intended oracle behavior to any implementation under test.

## Impact

This invalidates causal measurement for S1-S4 because a model or deterministic baseline can infer the expected branch/reframe/closure class from the fixture label rather than from domain semantics/evidence. The existing `phase1_v1` freeze is still useful as a qualification/regression set, but it must not be treated as the measurement holdout.

## Resolution approach

- Preserve `phase1_v1` unchanged as a qualification/regression generation.
- Create a new measurement generation (`phase1_v2`) with no oracle-revealing scenario labels or author notes in model-visible input.
- Keep scenario/category metadata only in hidden manifest/evaluation metadata.
- Freeze v2 before any LLM-vs-EC measurements.
- Add a TCC leakage gate that rejects model-visible fields containing oracle category names or expected closure/reframe labels.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No model-visible input contains scenario-class labels, expected branch IDs, reframe expectation, or closure expectation.
2. Hidden evaluation metadata preserves fixture taxonomy.
3. A leakage scanner returns PASS across all measurement fixtures.
4. `phase1_v1` results are never mixed with v2 measurement results.
5. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase 1 blocker: S3 upstream artifact lacks ECv4.4 framing state
issues.body:
## Found during

Attempt to execute the Phase 1 v2 S3 Selection/Reframing layer with the latest ECv4.4 control path.

## Finding

The coarse contract says S3 consumes `candidate_set + semantic state`, but the current S1/S2 artifacts do not persist the ECv4.4 framing state required by `EC_V4_4_RESIDUAL_DETECTOR_V1` / framing evolution:

- framing variables
- dependency edges
- goal coverage
- observations/evidence bindings
- abstraction/facet metadata where applicable

The S1 artifact currently models entities/rules/goals, and S2 models candidate transitions, but there is no canonical adapter/state contract that maps them into ECv4.4 framing control.

## Impact

A direct ECv4.4 S3 run would require hidden/manual reconstruction of framing state, violating the controlled-intervention rule. Reframing accuracy could not be attributed to EC vs LLM fairly.

## Required repair

1. Add an implementation-independent `semantic_state` artifact/section before S3 containing the minimum framing state required by ECv4.4.
2. Define a deterministic adapter from S1/S2 persisted artifacts to that state, or make the state a persisted upstream artifact with its own hash.
3. LLM and EC S3 variants must consume the identical semantic-state hash.
4. Do not include expected reframe/closure labels in that state.
5. TCC must verify that S3 comparison runs share the same candidate-set and semantic-state hashes.

## Acceptance criteria

- ECv4.4 S3 can execute without reading hidden oracle metadata.
- No manual reconstruction is needed per fixture.
- Reframe-required and no-reframe cases are expressible from visible upstream state.
- State hash is frozen before S3 measurement.
- GitHub Actions remain disabled.
